title: The Hidden City Inside an Ant Colony
hook: What if a single insect could build a city that rivals humanity?
script: What if a single insect could build a city that rivals humanity? Ants are eusocial insects whose colonies can range from a few dozen individuals to millions. Nearly all ant colonies include one or more fertile females called queens, along with fertile males called drones. Most colony members are sterile, wingless female workers called ergates. Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females, most of which are workers, as well as soldiers and other specialised groups. Some colonies occupy large territories with sizeable nests, and supercolonies can reach hundreds of millions of individuals. In some lineages, such as army ants, the colony does not construct a permanent nest and moves almost incessantly. Ant colonies are described as superorganisms because the ants appear to operate as a unified entity. Ants have colonised almost every landmass on Earth; the only places lacking indigenous ants are Antarctica and a few remote or inhospitable islands. Their highly organised colonies remind us that the smallest lives can build complex societies.
